tools.name: resolve-library-id
tools.title: Resolve Context7 Library ID
tools.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

libraryName.description: Library name to search for and retrieve a Context7-compatible library ID. Use the official library name with proper punctuation — e.g., 'Next.js' instead of 'nextjs', 'Customer.io' instead of 'customerio', 'Three.js' instead of 'threejs'.

tools.name: query-docs
tools.title: Query Documentation
tools.description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation, scoped to a single concept. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the user's question spans multiple distinct concepts, make a separate call per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad (too vague): 'auth' or 'hooks'. Bad (too broad): 'routing and auth and caching in Next.js'. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

### Parse JSON Request Body

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/08-advanced-topics.md

Use the built-in `express.json()` middleware to automatically parse incoming JSON request bodies into `req.body`.

```javascript
app.post('/api/users', express.json(), (req, res) => {
  const { name, email } = req.body
  res.json({ name, email })
})
```

--------------------------------

### Parsing JSON Request Bodies with express.json()

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/07-middleware-and-routing.md

Use `express.json()` to parse incoming request bodies with a JSON content type. It populates `req.body` with the parsed JSON object. Options like `limit` can control the maximum request size.

```javascript
app.use(express.json())
app.use(express.json({ limit: '10mb' }))
```

```javascript
app.post('/api/users', express.json(), (req, res) => {
  console.log(req.body)  // Parsed JSON
  res.json({ success: true })
})
```

--------------------------------

### express.json([options])

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/06-types-and-configuration.md

Middleware that parses incoming requests with JSON payloads.

```APIDOC
## express.json([options])

### Description
Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads.

### Parameters
- **strict** (boolean) - Optional - Only parse objects and arrays. Default: true
- **type** (string | Array) - Optional - Content-Type to parse. Default: 'application/json'
- **limit** (string | number) - Optional - Request body size limit. Default: '100kb'
- **verify** (Function) - Optional - Verification callback.
- **charset** (string) - Optional - Charset to use. Default: 'utf-8'

### Example
```javascript
app.use(express.json({
  strict: false,
  limit: '10mb',
  type: ['application/json', 'application/csp-report']
}))
```
```

--------------------------------

### Use Built-in Middleware

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/00-index.md

Standard middleware functions provided by Express for parsing bodies and serving static files.

```javascript
express.json(options)
express.urlencoded(options)
express.text(options)
express.raw(options)
express.static(root, options)
```

### Middleware Configuration > express.json([options])

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/06-types-and-configuration.md

The built-in `express.json()` middleware parses incoming JSON request bodies. Key options include `strict` (default: true) to only parse objects and arrays, `type` to specify Content-Types, `limit` for request body size, and `verify` for a custom verification callback.

@app.post("/items/")

### Declare Common Query Parameters with Function Dependency

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/classes-as-dependencies

Use a function with default and optional parameters as a shared dependency across multiple route handlers.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


async def common_parameters(q: str | None = None, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return {"q": q, "skip": skip, "limit": limit}


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(commons: Annotated[dict, Depends(common_parameters)]):
    return commons


@app.get("/users/")
async def read_users(commons: Annotated[dict, Depends(common_parameters)]):
    return commons

```

### Declare Inline Depends Parameter

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes

### Declare dependency with Annotated in FastAPI

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies

Define a reusable dependency function using `Annotated` and `Depends` in FastAPI path operations. This method ensures type information is preserved for better tooling support.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


async def common_parameters(q: str | None = None, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return {"q": q, "skip": skip, "limit": limit}


@app.get("/items/")

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/sub-dependencies

### HttpRequest.get_host() — incoming Host header validation

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/http/request.py

Validates the incoming HTTP Host header against ALLOWED_HOSTS. When DEBUG=True and ALLOWED_HOSTS is empty, defaults to [".localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"]. Raises DisallowedHost if the incoming host does not match. This is the primary gate preventing Host header injection attacks.

```python
def get_host(self):
    """Return the HTTP host using the environment or request headers."""
    host = self._get_raw_host()

    # Allow variants of localhost if ALLOWED_HOSTS is empty and DEBUG=True.
    allowed_hosts = settings.ALLOWED_HOSTS
    if settings.DEBUG and not allowed_hosts:
        allowed_hosts = [".localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"]

    domain, port = split_domain_port(host)
    if domain and validate_host(domain, allowed_hosts):
        return host
    else:
        msg = "Invalid HTTP_HOST header: %r." % host
        if domain:
            msg += " You may need to add %r to ALLOWED_HOSTS." % domain
        else:
            msg += (
                " The domain name provided is not valid according to RFC 1034/1035."
            )
        raise DisallowedHost(msg)
```

--------------------------------

### Basic Django Settings Configuration

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/topics/settings.md

Example settings file showing common configuration variables like ALLOWED_HOSTS, DEBUG, and DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL. These are module-level variables in a Python settings file.

```python
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["www.example.com"]
DEBUG = False
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL = "webmaster@example.com"
```

--------------------------------

### Nginx Configuration for Host Validation

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/howto/deployment/checklist.md

Configure Nginx to validate the Host header and reject requests for unrecognized hosts. This is a crucial step to prevent CSRF attacks when DEBUG is False.

```nginx
server {
    listen 80 default_server;
    return 444;
}
```

### Settings > Core Settings > ALLOWED_HOSTS

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/ref/settings.txt

ALLOWED_HOSTS defines a list of strings representing the host or domain names the Django site can serve, acting as a security measure against HTTP Host header attacks. Values can be fully qualified domain names, subdomain wildcards starting with a period, or '*' to match anything. If a host does not match and DEBUG is False, HttpRequest.get_host() raises SuspiciousOperation; if DEBUG is True and the list is empty, it defaults to validating against localhost and loopback addresses.

--------------------------------

### DEBUG

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/ref/settings.md

The DEBUG setting enables debug mode, displaying detailed error pages and metadata when exceptions occur, while automatically hiding sensitive settings containing substrings like API, KEY, PASS, SECRET, SIGNATURE, or TOKEN. DEBUG should never be enabled in production because it exposes server internals and logs every executed SQL query in memory. When DEBUG is False, the ALLOWED_HOSTS setting must be configured to prevent 400 Bad Request errors.

### Actuator Endpoints Overview

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/api/rest/actuator/index.html

This section details the base URL structure for Actuator endpoints and how to configure it. By default, endpoints are accessed under `/actuator/{id}`. The base path can be customized using the `management.endpoints.web.base-path` property.

```APIDOC
## Actuator Endpoints

### Description
Provides access to various Actuator endpoints for monitoring and management.

### Base Path Configuration
By default, all web endpoints are available beneath the path `/actuator` with URLs of the form `/actuator/{id}`. The `/actuator` base path can be configured by using the `management.endpoints.web.base-path` property.

**Example Configuration:**
```properties
management.endpoints.web.base-path=/manage
```

This configuration changes the endpoint URLs from `/actuator/{id}` to `/manage/{id}`. For example, the `info` endpoint would become `/manage/info`.
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Actuator Base Path

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/api/rest/actuator/index.html

Change the base path for all web endpoints from the default `/actuator` to a custom path. This affects all endpoint URLs.

```properties
management.endpoints.web.base-path=/manage
```

--------------------------------

### Customize Management Endpoint Base Path

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/actuator/monitoring.html

Change the prefix for all management endpoints from `/actuator` to `/manage`. This applies to properties and YAML configurations.

```properties
management.endpoints.web.base-path=/manage
```

```yaml
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      base-path: "/manage"
```

### Actuator Properties

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/appendix/application-properties/index.html

The `management.endpoints.web.base-path` property configures the base path for web-accessible Actuator endpoints. When the management server shares the main server port, this path is relative to the servlet context path or WebFlux base path. If a separate management server port is configured, it's relative to the management server's base path. The default is `/actuator`.

--------------------------------

### Actuator REST API > URLs

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/api/rest/actuator/index.html

All web endpoints are available under the `/actuator` path by default, with URLs following the pattern `/actuator/{id}`. This base path can be customized using the `management.endpoints.web.base-path` property.

### Parse JSON Request Body

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/08-advanced-topics.md

Use the built-in `express.json()` middleware to automatically parse incoming JSON request bodies into `req.body`.

```javascript
app.post('/api/users', express.json(), (req, res) => {
  const { name, email } = req.body
  res.json({ name, email })
})
```

--------------------------------

### Parsing JSON Request Bodies with express.json()

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/07-middleware-and-routing.md

Use `express.json()` to parse incoming request bodies with a JSON content type. It populates `req.body` with the parsed JSON object. Options like `limit` can control the maximum request size.

```javascript
app.use(express.json())
app.use(express.json({ limit: '10mb' }))
```

```javascript
app.post('/api/users', express.json(), (req, res) => {
  console.log(req.body)  // Parsed JSON
  res.json({ success: true })
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure express.json middleware

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/06-types-and-configuration.md

Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads using custom options.

```javascript
app.use(express.json({
  strict: false,
  limit: '10mb',
  type: ['application/json', 'application/csp-report']
}))
```

--------------------------------

### express.json([options])

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/06-types-and-configuration.md

Middleware that parses incoming requests with JSON payloads.

```APIDOC
## express.json([options])

### Description
Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads.

### Parameters
- **strict** (boolean) - Optional - Only parse objects and arrays. Default: true
- **type** (string | Array) - Optional - Content-Type to parse. Default: 'application/json'
- **limit** (string | number) - Optional - Request body size limit. Default: '100kb'
- **verify** (Function) - Optional - Verification callback.
- **charset** (string) - Optional - Charset to use. Default: 'utf-8'

### Example
```javascript
app.use(express.json({
  strict: false,
  limit: '10mb',
  type: ['application/json', 'application/csp-report']
}))
```
```

--------------------------------

### Add Middleware with app.use()

Source: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/master/_autodocs/02-application-api.md

Use `app.use()` to add middleware functions or mount other Express applications. It can accept a path, a single middleware function, an array of functions, or a combination.

```javascript
app.use(fn)
app.use('/path', fn)
app.use([fn, fn2, ...])
app.use('/path', [fn, fn2, ...])
```

```javascript
const app = express()

app.use(express.json())

app.use('/api', apiRouter)

app.use((req, res, next) => {
  console.log(req.method, req.path)
  next()
})

const subapp = express()
subapp.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Sub'))
app.use('/sub', subapp)
```

content.text:
### Declare Dependencies with Default Parameter Syntax

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes

Demonstrates path operation functions declaring dependencies directly as parameter default values before Annotated support.

```python
def get_current_user(token: str):
    # authenticate user
    return User()


@app.get("/items/")
def read_items(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    ...


@app.post("/items/")
def create_item(*, user: User = Depends(get_current_user), item: Item):
    ...


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(*, user: User = Depends(get_current_user), item_id: int):
    ...


@app.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(*, user: User = Depends(get_current_user), item_id: int):
    ...

```

--------------------------------

### Declare Common Query Parameters with Function Dependency

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/classes-as-dependencies

Use a function with default and optional parameters as a shared dependency across multiple route handlers.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


async def common_parameters(q: str | None = None, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return {"q": q, "skip": skip, "limit": limit}


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(commons: Annotated[dict, Depends(common_parameters)]):
    return commons


@app.get("/users/")
async def read_users(commons: Annotated[dict, Depends(common_parameters)]):
    return commons

```

```python
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


async def common_parameters(q: str | None = None, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return {"q": q, "skip": skip, "limit": limit}


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(commons: dict = Depends(common_parameters)):
    return commons


@app.get("/users/")
async def read_users(commons: dict = Depends(common_parameters)):
    return commons

```

--------------------------------

### Declare Inline Depends Parameter

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes

Shows the standard single-line syntax for defining a parameter dependency using default values.

```python
user: User = Depends(get_current_user)

```

--------------------------------

### Reuse Annotated Dependency in Path Operations

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes

Demonstrates sharing a single Annotated dependency type across multiple path operation functions to eliminate parameter duplication.

```python
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]


@app.get("/items/")
def read_items(user: CurrentUser):
    ...


@app.post("/items/")
def create_item(user: CurrentUser, item: Item):
    ...


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(user: CurrentUser, item_id: int):
    ...


@app.delete("/items/{item_id}")
def delete_item(user: CurrentUser, item_id: int):
    ...

```

--------------------------------

### fastapi.Depends

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/reference/dependencies

Declares a FastAPI dependency callable to be executed automatically by FastAPI during request handling.

```APIDOC
## fastapi.Depends

### Description
Declare a FastAPI dependency. It takes a single "dependable" callable (like a function). Rather than calling it directly, pass the callable object to FastAPI to invoke it during request handling.

### Signature
`Depends(dependency=None, *, use_cache=True, scope=None)`

### Parameters
- **dependency** (`Callable[..., Any] | None`, optional, default: `None`) - A "dependable" callable (like a function). Do not call it directly; pass the object directly so FastAPI can invoke it.
- **use_cache** (`bool`, optional, default: `True`) - By default, after a dependency is called the first time in a request, re-declarations within the same request re-use the cached value. Set to `False` to force re-execution.
- **scope** (`str | None`, optional, default: `None`) - Mainly for dependencies with `yield`, defines when the dependency starts and ends:
  - `"function"`: Runs before the path operation function and ends after the function completes, but before the response is sent.
  - `"request"`: Runs before the path operation function and ends after the response has been sent back to the client.

### Usage Example
```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

async def common_parameters(q: str | None = None, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return {"q": q, "skip": skip, "limit": limit}

@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(commons: Annotated[dict, Depends(common_parameters)]):
    return commons
```
```

### HttpRequest.get_host() — incoming Host header validation

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/http/request.py

Validates the incoming HTTP Host header against ALLOWED_HOSTS. When DEBUG=True and ALLOWED_HOSTS is empty, defaults to [".localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"]. Raises DisallowedHost if the incoming host does not match. This is the primary gate preventing Host header injection attacks.

```python
def get_host(self):
    """Return the HTTP host using the environment or request headers."""
    host = self._get_raw_host()

    # Allow variants of localhost if ALLOWED_HOSTS is empty and DEBUG=True.
    allowed_hosts = settings.ALLOWED_HOSTS
    if settings.DEBUG and not allowed_hosts:
        allowed_hosts = [".localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"]

    domain, port = split_domain_port(host)
    if domain and validate_host(domain, allowed_hosts):
        return host
    else:
        msg = "Invalid HTTP_HOST header: %r." % host
        if domain:
            msg += " You may need to add %r to ALLOWED_HOSTS." % domain
        else:
            msg += (
                " The domain name provided is not valid according to RFC 1034/1035."
            )
        raise DisallowedHost(msg)
```

--------------------------------

### Basic Django Settings Configuration

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/topics/settings.md

Example settings file showing common configuration variables like ALLOWED_HOSTS, DEBUG, and DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL. These are module-level variables in a Python settings file.

```python
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["www.example.com"]
DEBUG = False
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL = "webmaster@example.com"
```

### Settings > Core Settings > ALLOWED_HOSTS

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/ref/settings.txt

ALLOWED_HOSTS defines a list of strings representing the host or domain names the Django site can serve, acting as a security measure against HTTP Host header attacks. Values can be fully qualified domain names, subdomain wildcards starting with a period, or '*' to match anything. If a host does not match and DEBUG is False, HttpRequest.get_host() raises SuspiciousOperation; if DEBUG is True and the list is empty, it defaults to validating against localhost and loopback addresses.

--------------------------------

### Environment-specific settings > ALLOWED_HOSTS

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/howto/deployment/checklist.txt

When `DEBUG = False`, `ALLOWED_HOSTS` must be set correctly to protect against CSRF attacks. Configure your web server to validate the host and handle incorrect hosts appropriately to avoid Django errors.

--------------------------------

### DEBUG

Source: https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/docs/ref/settings.md

The DEBUG setting enables debug mode, displaying detailed error pages and metadata when exceptions occur, while automatically hiding sensitive settings containing substrings like API, KEY, PASS, SECRET, SIGNATURE, or TOKEN. DEBUG should never be enabled in production because it exposes server internals and logs every executed SQL query in memory. When DEBUG is False, the ALLOWED_HOSTS setting must be configured to prevent 400 Bad Request errors.

### Configure Actuator Base Path

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.5/api/rest/actuator/index.html

Use this property in application.properties to change the default base path for all web endpoints.

```properties
management.endpoints.web.base-path=/manage
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Management Base Path

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.5/reference/actuator/monitoring.html

Changes the default management endpoint prefix from /actuator to /manage.

```properties
management.endpoints.web.base-path=/manage
```

```yaml
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      base-path: "/manage"
```

--------------------------------

### Remap Specific Endpoint Paths

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.5/reference/actuator/monitoring.html

Changes the path for a specific endpoint, such as mapping /actuator/health to /healthcheck.

```properties
management.endpoints.web.base-path=/
management.endpoints.web.path-mapping.health=healthcheck
```

```yaml
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      base-path: "/"
      path-mapping:
        health: "healthcheck"
```

### Customizing the Management Endpoint Paths

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.5/reference/actuator/monitoring.html

You can customize the base prefix for management endpoints by using the management.endpoints.web.base-path property. This is useful if the default /actuator path conflicts with existing application routes. By default, this path is relative to the server context path or the reactive web base path, unless a specific management port is configured.

--------------------------------

### URLs

Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.5/api/rest/actuator/index.html

By default, all web endpoints are accessible under the /actuator path using the format /actuator/{id}. This base path can be customized by modifying the management.endpoints.web.base-path property to suit specific application routing requirements.
